$comment: M8 machine-readable member inventory (Wave 1 deliverable). One row per current public leaf, target public leaf, and public handle leaf, enumerated from implementation facts: lib/plugin-api-service.js disabled/conditional surfaces, lib/client-runtime.js composition, and the per-domain slice modules. Field contract: publicPath, runtime, kind ('leaf'|'handle'), currentShape (null = no current counterpart), targetPath (null = deleted), idiom (one of the eight idioms, 'passthrough-exception', or null for deleted members with no target classification), migrationAction ('rename'|'merge'|'split'|'migrate'|'delete'|'internalize'|'retain'|'add'; 'add' marks a new target leaf with no current counterpart and must be reconciled into the registry namespace/member records in Wave 2), shapeNote (key current-to-target change; null when unchanged). Handle leaves use the '<parent>.handle.<member>' path convention; handle rows are handle-level entries whose observable members are listed in shapeNote, and member-level expansion lands in the Wave 2 leaf-level registry. Official forwarding leaves merged into the public surface by activated feature mounters (official llm/agent/session/settings/systemPrompt leaves) are enumerated with migrationAction 'migrate' to services.<domain> targets. The only symbol-keyed member observable on the public face is the non-enumerable session-channel contract marker, retained as an internal facade/replacement contract marker and not registered as a publicPath leaf. services.* passthrough members are reviewed in servicesWhitelistReview rather than enumerated leaf by leaf here; their member-level descriptors remain in the M7 registry servicesWhitelist, which is the single source they extend in Wave 2.

host.note: All 46 audited host service keys are retained as passthrough-exception members. Facade semantic claims are prohibited on these members. Member-level retain/remove decisions stay in the M7 registry servicesWhitelist member descriptors, which M8 extends in place with registry metadata (publicPath, implementationChannel passthrough, composition, authority, bypasses, visibility, cancellation, availability). Migration targets services.recovery and services.tools, plus the official-forwarding targets services.llm / services.agents / services.sessions / services.settings / services.prompts, are Wave 2 whitelist extension candidates.

client.note: Official browser services are exposed only through audited services.* paths. The seven passthrough leaves ride under services.* with caller-bound resolution; remaining official browser service keys stay under services.<key>.

gapResolution.note: All leaves above were resolved from implementation facts (disabled/conditional surface mirrors, composition code, and per-domain slice modules). Three capability gaps are carried into the capability matrix rather than resolved as active members: (1) the owner-scoped custom event publisher (events.define) is unavailable because the current runtime cannot enforce owner scope — it is neither a current nor a target leaf and is recorded as an unavailable/proposal capability only; (2) consultation-style entries (executions.recovery.consume, security.egress.check) are deleted and their capability conservation depends on automatic application evidence, otherwise they are recorded as gaps. The non-enumerable session-channel contract marker symbol on the channels surface is an internal facade/replacement contract marker, not a publicPath leaf; Wave 7 reconciliation treats it as internal. The tool-skill contract marker lives on the ctx.skillActivation service object, outside the pluginApi public face. Wave 2 validator note: passthrough-exception on migrate rows is judged by targetPath (services.*) rather than currentPath, matching the standard inventory table.
gapResolution.blockedConsumerVerification: Consumer headless smoke and dev boot depend on the consumer repositories' node_modules/@deepseek-ai resolution path; if the official shared install tree remains unwritable, they are recorded as blocked per the M7 precedent.
